correctness.rationale: The binary proof's alphabet-sensitive steps were isolated and transferred: q-ary k-unique words remain a constant-density family; local edits remain disjoint {-1,0,1} bubbles when boundary symbols are merely unequal to the edited symbol; exceptional records gain q^O_t(1); and witness descriptions gain q^O_t(R), which is absorbed into the hash range without changing the n^(2t-1) exponent. Finite checks report PASS.

originality.rationale: The inspected motivating preprint explicitly leaves the fixed-larger-alphabet 2t-1 coefficient as open. Targeted external searches found q-ary deletion constructions with larger leading coefficients or different burst/read models, but no ordinary q-ary t-deletion theorem with this coefficient. SCOPE overlap searches found no matching record. Near-simultaneous and folklore risk remain material.

value.rationale: The result resolves a stated open extension of a new deletion-code bound and shows that the one-factor-of-n gain over the greedy existential estimate is alphabet-independent. In particular, fixed q-ary two-deletion codes exist with leading bit-redundancy coefficient 3 rather than the generic coefficient 4.
